context: Sho hesitates to share a toy and Hina suggests sharing.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ひな、これ、ぼくの、おもちゃ。
lines.style: Soft, careful opening. A small boy protecting something precious. The words come slowly, each one genuine. Warm underneath the hesitation, the kind of honesty only a six-year-old can give.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: ちょっと、貸してくれる？
lines.en: Can I borrow it for a bit?
lines.style: Bright, hopeful lift. Eight-year-old warmth and eagerness. The question carries genuine curiosity and trust. Real childish sincerity — no performance, just asking.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Quiet agreement, no hesitation. A small affirmative that carries the weight of choosing to share something that matters. Tender acceptance, the real gentleness of a child saying yes to someone he likes.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: Playing together like this is really fun.
lines.style: Genuine delight. Bright and unselfconscious. The realization said out loud without embarrassment — eight-year-old enthusiasm that's sincere, not performed. Warm wonder in the voice.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Small, steady voice. A six-year-old saying something true and important. The words arrive without fanfare but with real weight. Deep tenderness — the quiet certainty of a child who has learned what kindness feels like.
